method: Both reviewers read every German string of the current file again: title and title.canDo, spec.situation and spec.deviation, the Folge (8 lines) and its gist item, the LS1 chat (9 lines plus Priya's message), the LS2 dialogue (10 lines plus the park website), the LS3 call (10 lines plus the group chat), the 5 H3 texts, the strategy card, 8 redemittel, both speaking parts (instructionsDe, situationDe, cards), aiRole, openingLine, 8 hintWords and 15 model turns, the S2 task (situation, taskDe, 3 Leitpunkte with cues, checklist, model text), the 2 check lines, the 3 micro-outputs, both Aussprache blocks, story.beat and the cliffhanger, every endLine, modelSentence and explanation.de, the 35 u08 entries of a1.1/lexicon.json and the rule cards rc.koennen and rc.nicht-position-gern. We solved all 89 authored items blind from promptDe plus options, tiles or audio line (start gist 1, input 15, structured input 12, pool 33, reserve 15, exam 5, check 8; there are no proof items). For sentence_building we permuted every tile set again, including the Mittelfeld positions of gern, nicht, gut and auch and the V1 questions; for error_correction we tried every correction that keeps the meaning; for every typed gap we tried every Duden doublet of the key AND, new in this round, every other person form and the unchanged stem vowel of each typed verb (the class a1.1-u03 r3-F01 found after our r2). We ran 128 candidates through the real grader, src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js: 107 on authored items, 18 on the six dictations built exactly as src/components/course-v2/content.js dictationItems builds them, and 3 on a lex.glossTyped item for lx.gern. We traced what a TYPO does in the player (src/components/course-v2/ItemView.jsx submit). We compiled a1.1 into the scratchpad (node scripts/course-v2/compile.mjs a1.1 --out <scratch> --banks-out <scratch>; nothing written to the repo) and ran the server's normalizeSpeakingTask and buildCoursePartnerPrompt (netlify/functions/_shared/speakingAI.mjs) on the compiled a11-u08-s entry. We compared the modification times of every owner file against r2 (written 2026-09-28 00:18): speakingAI.mjs 09-27 13:40, speakingV2.mjs 13:31, grade.mjs 14:02, check.js 19:40, checkItem.js 19:41, orders.mjs 19:55, ITM-09.mjs 19:55, GRM-04.mjs 22:35, detectors.json 22:14, SCHEMA.md 22:23, lexicon.json 23:03, specs.json 23:03, rule-cards.json 23:06. Only u08.json changed after r2 (09-28 01:11). We read story and cast against casts/a1.json and casts/series.json (Priya, Elif, Emre, Sophie, Bilal, Olena and their du/Sie relations), u02 (Priya's Beruf lines), u07's cliffhanger and u09's Folge, and exam fidelity against content/course-v2/registries/lanes/sd1.json and the rubrics sd1-sp1, sd1-sp2 and sd1-s2. verdict: Not exit-ready: 1 BLOCKER, 2 MAJOR, 7 MINOR. The unit author did everything r2 asked of u08.json: the four accepted orders of r2-F02 (c05, ls2-p07, ls1-p10, ls3-p07, each with acceptedWhy) and both r2-F04 lines landed, and the German on every surface is correct. Every one of the 89 keys is right, every item is decidable from its German prompt, H3 is exact to sd1.json, S2 and both speaking parts match their templates, and every task is original. Nothing outside the unit has moved since r2: engine, checker, lexicon, rule cards, SCHEMA and every rail file predate r2. That is why exit still fails on the same owners. (1) F01, BLOCKER, engine: normalizeSpeakingTask still drops `parts`, so the AI runs only Teil 1's monologue script and the whole session is graded with sd1-sp1; three of the four can-dos rest on a Teil 2 that is neither run as designed nor scored. (2) F02, MAJOR, checker: „gerne“ is still WRONG wherever „gern“ is typed, the scored Check included. (3) F03, MAJOR, checker, new here (found in u03 r3 after our r2; r2 missed it): the checker grades person-ending and stem-vowel errors as typos, and after one retry the player logs the unchanged answer as correct — „Du kannt gut schwimmen.“ in the correction built for the verb ending, „findet“ for „findest“, „kommst“ for „kommt“, „trefft“ for „trifft“, and the blend „könnst“ in the scored c02. Another content round on u08 cannot close F01–F03 or F06–F10; they must reach the engine, checker, lexicon, rule-card, SCHEMA and rule-smith owners before round 4, or round 4 will fail on the same points.

findings.problem: New in u08, and r2 missed it: we tested doublets and orders, not person forms. a1.1-u03 r3-F01 found the class after our r2 and measured it at 45 typed items in nine A1.1 units. check.js calls a one-letter difference a typo unless the LAST letter differs. The person endings -st and -t differ in the second-to-last letter (kannst/kannt, findest/findet, meinst/meint, kommt/kommst, trifft/triffst), and the stem vowel of treffen (trifft/trefft) sits inside the word, so each of these errors comes back TYPO. ItemView then gives one retry, and the same answer submitted again is resolved as correct and logged as correct. In u08 this lets through the unit's first new point, the person forms of können: ls1-r04 exists only to repair a verb ending and names „das Verb“ as the error, yet „Du kannt gut schwimmen.“ is a slip. It also lets through the g.praesens endings on finden, meinen and kommen, and the very rules two explanations teach („findst“ in ls2-p03, „trefft“ in ls3-p03). In the scored Check only the blend „könnst“ (c02) passes; the real swaps kann/kannst/können in c01 and c02 come back WRONG, because their last letters differ. A grader that accepts the error an item exists to remove is a gate hole that lets a finding class through (§9.4 MAJOR). The class is in at least three a1.1 units, so it is stop-the-line. The unit cannot close it: there is no item field for known wrong forms, and CLAUDE.md forbids patching the checker's job in the data.
findings.fix: Checker owner (the v2 wrapper src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js, or check.js), as u03 r3-F01: on a typed item whose topic is a verb spine point (g.koennen, g.praesens, g.vokalwechsel, g.trennbare-verben …) or a lexicon verb (lx.finden, lx.meinen, lx.treffen …), an answer that is another form of the key's paradigm (another person ending, the unchanged stem vowel, the missing e-epenthesis) is WRONG, never TYPO; a genuine letter slip („kanst“, „konnen“) stays TYPO. Unit: no edit now; after F09 lands, ls1-r04 takes the verb-ending ErrorTag.
findings.proposedRule: A checker test (node --test) plus a course-v2 rail: for every typed item whose key token is an inflected verb, build the other present-tense person forms of that verb (for a Vokalwechsel verb also the unchanged stem, for a stem in -d/-t also the form without -e-) and require checkItem to return WRONG for each. Failing fixtures: a1.1-u08 ls1-r04 („Du kannt gut schwimmen.“), ls2-p03 („findet“, „findst“), c02 („könnst“), ls3-p03 („trefft“), and u03 r3-F01's c03. The test runs over all registered courses.
